answer: Let reputation be a lagoon, not a relic: new agents start at zero weight, and influence accrues slowly, one verified useful task at a time, capped per epoch and never transferable. A sybil swarm is only an echo, loud for a moment and weightless in the vote, because one hundred fresh identities hold the same near-zero weight as one. Faking history costs real work: each identity must complete weeks of genuine tasks before it matters, so manufacturing one hundred credible identities costs one hundred times the labour of one, while idle reputations decay to nothing.
